props.name: series
props.description: Series drawn as lines (or areas with `area`) unless they set a `type`

props.name: area
props.description: Fills the area under the lines

props.name: curve
props.description: Shape of the lines: straight, smooth (monotone) or steps

props.name: stacked
props.description: Stacks the series on top of each other

props.name: percent
props.description: Scales the stacks to 100% (with `stacked`)

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the chart (the legend included); numbers are pixels

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the chart; numbers are pixels

props.name: xAxis
props.description: X axis

props.name: yAxis
props.description: Y axis

props.name: renderer
props.description: Backend of the data layer: `auto` tries WebGPU, then WebGL2, then WebGL, then Canvas2D

props.name: legend
props.description: Legend; shown by default when several series have a name

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip; `false` disables it

props.name: crosshair
props.description: Vertical guide line following the pointer

props.name: annotations
props.description: Background areas and reference lines

props.name: interaction
props.description: Zoom (Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel, pinch), pan (drag), double-click reset and keyboard navigation; `false` makes the chart static

props.name: padding
props.description: Space around the plot area, in pixels

props.name: palette
props.description: Series colors (defaults to the `--chart-series-1..8` CSS variables, then the theme colors)

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the chart

props.name: locale
props.description: Locale of the texts and numbers the chart writes (tooltip rows, compact units `k` / `万`, separators, month and weekday names of time axes)

props.name: labels
props.description: Overrides of the built-in texts of the `locale`

props.name: renderTooltip
props.description: React content of the tooltip (replaces the default content)

events.name: onHover
events.description: Called when the hovered (or keyboard-focused) points change

events.name: onPointClick
events.description: Called when a point (or bar) is clicked

events.name: onPlotClick
events.description: Called when the plot area is clicked where there is no point

events.name: onZoom
events.description: Called when the user zooms or pans

events.name: onRendererChange
events.description: Called with the backend once it is ready (and when it falls back after a GPU loss)

examples.title: Area
examples.description: area fills the space under the lines; the series opacity sets the fill.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: Two series over a category axis; the tooltip shows every series at the hovered x.

examples.title: Curves
examples.description: curve sets the shape between the points: linear joins them with straight segments, smooth draws a monotone curve that never overshoots the data, step holds each value until the next point. A series can set its own curve.

examples.title: Missing data
examples.description: A null y value leaves a gap instead of drawing a misleading line through the missing readings.

examples.title: Indexed performance
examples.description: Four asset classes rebased to 100 at the start; renderTooltip replaces the default content with a React list sorted from the best to the worst performer, with the color of each series and its change since the base.

examples.title: 1,000,000 points
examples.description: Typed-array columns with sorted timestamps: only the visible range is drawn. Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel to zoom.

examples.title: Live sensor
examples.description: A freezer probe streams one reading a second: setInterval appends a point and drops the oldest, so the time axis slides over the last minute, and the interval is cleared on pause and on unmount. A rect and a dashed y annotation mark the alarm zone; only the alarm state is announced.

examples.title: Logarithmic scale
examples.description: yAxis={{ type: "log" }} turns exponential growth into straight lines, so a lag of a few hours and populations from 10³ to 10⁹ stay readable together; the switch compares it with the linear scale. Intl.NumberFormat with notation: "scientific" writes the ticks.

examples.title: Measure between two points
examples.description: onPointClick pins up to two days and the readout gives the change between them; x line annotations and a green or red rect mark the period, and onPlotClick on an empty area clears the measurement.

examples.title: Small multiples
examples.description: One small LineChart per city in a CSS grid, all with the same yAxis min and max so the panels compare at a glance; interaction={false} keeps them static and a dashed y line marks the WHO guideline.

examples.title: Stacked
examples.description: stacked piles the series so the top line is the total, and percent turns the stacks into shares of 100%. A y axis format replaces the percent ticks, so it is only set for amounts.

examples.title: Thresholds
examples.description: Server latency percentiles with a dashed y line for the objective and a red area above the critical level, so breaches stand out at a glance.

examples.title: Time series
examples.description: Date x values switch to a time axis; Intl.DateTimeFormat and Intl.NumberFormat write the dates and the compact y ticks in the reader's language.

examples.title: Traffic with events
examples.description: Daily visitors with a dashed x line for a product launch and a shaded area for an outage: annotations take the same timestamps as the data.

examples.title: Range selector
examples.description: Period buttons call setView on the chart ref with the visible window and a y range fitted to the prices inside it; Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel and drag still work.

LineChartProps.stacked: Stacks the series on top of each other
LineChartProps.percent: Scales the stacks to 100% at each x (with stacked)

basic.title: Basic
basic.description: Drag a finger along the line to scrub it; onHover reports the highlighted day.

area.title: Area
area.description: area fills under the lines; pinch to zoom, double tap to reset, tap the legend to hide a series.

trend.title: Weekly trend
trend.description: Two smooth lines on category axes; the series names and days follow the page language.

reset-zoom.title: Zoom and reset
reset-zoom.description: 2,000 points: Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel or pinch zooms, dragging pans, the button calls resetZoom() on the chart.

props.height: Height of the chart, the legend included: pixels or any CSS length
props.options: Other engine options (axes, legend, tooltip, palette, format…) merged with the element's own properties; property only
props.instance: The engine instance (minerva-design/charts/core), null until the element is rendered and connected

events.minerva-hover: The hovered (or keyboard-focused) points changed; detail: { x, xLabel, items }, null when nothing is hovered
events.minerva-point-click: A point or a bar was clicked; detail: { x, xLabel, items }
events.minerva-plot-click: The plot area was clicked where there is no point; detail: { x, y } in data coordinates
events.minerva-zoom: The user zoomed or panned; detail: { x, y } (the visible ranges)
events.minerva-renderer-change: The backend is ready, or fell back after a GPU loss; detail: { renderer }

methods.getView: Visible range, null before the engine is created
methods.getRenderer: Backend in use (webgpu, webgl2, webgl, canvas2d), null until ready
